narrative: OMX30 enters Friday supported by broad European strength and positive overnight signals from US equities (Dow +1.08%, S&P +0.33%) despite NASDAQ flatness. Copper's explosive +1.77% move and gold's +0.69% gain provide tailwinds for Boliden and broader materials exposure. Technicals remain constructive—the index trades +4.6% above its 200-MA with MACD above signal and robust 90-day momentum (+7.3%)—though ADX's weakness (3.0) signals a lack of trending conviction. USD/SEK's decline to 9.885 marginally benefits exporters in a crowded positioning, while a 1.95% drop in US 10Y yields (now 5.089%) is mixed: banks get NIM support, but tech faces DCF headwinds. Key risk: late-week USD strength reversal or trade war escalation headlines could derail the fragile rally.
morningBrief: OMX30 set for modest upside today on DAX coattails and commodity strength—target +0.4–0.5% on open. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken, Swedbank) are core long on yield floor and NIM stability; watch for 50-MA at 3180 as near-term resistance. Boliden is the day's star: copper +1.77% and gold +0.69% should drive earnings revisions higher—strong buy. Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Sandvik) steady beneficiaries of subdued USD/SEK, though monitor for geopolitical spillover from Trump headlines. NASDAQ's flatness is a minor drag on Ericsson and Hexagon; avoid chasing unless sentiment shifts decisively. Support at 3085 (lower Bollinger); if VIX spikes above 18, expect reversal. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is the day's only event risk. Stochastic at 72 signals neutral momentum; do not chase momentum—scale into strength.
